analysis.investment_thesis: Aarti Industries is a classic cycle-peak-to-bust story: net profit collapsed from INR 1,186 Cr in FY22 to INR 331 Cr in FY25 while the stock still trades at 43x P/E and 18.4x EV/EBITDA on the hope of a specialty chemicals recovery. The price is paying for a recovery that may be years away while the underlying business earns a 6% ROE — that is an unacceptable risk/reward.
key_strengths: Established specialty chemicals platform with complex multi-step chemistry that creates some switching costs for pharma and agrochemical customers
Revenue base of INR 7,271 Cr with 10.3% CAGR over 9 years shows the business is not structurally broken
Debt/Equity at 0.70x is manageable; the company is not at existential risk
key_risks: Earnings have collapsed 72% from peak (INR 1,186 Cr FY22 → INR 331 Cr FY25) with contracting EBITDA trend — paying 43x P/E on trough earnings that may not recover to peak
Finance costs have nearly tripled (INR 86 Cr FY21 → INR 275 Cr FY25) while EBITDA stagnates; operating leverage works in reverse here
Free cash flow has been negative every year for 5 years; massive capex (CWIP of INR 1,596 Cr) risks value destruction if the capacity cycle overshoots demand
red_flags: ROE of only 6.03% at P/B of 2.81 — the business is earning roughly its cost of equity at best; there is no economic profit justifying this premium
Net profit CAGR of only 2.4% over 9 years while the stock has been priced as a growth compounder — a fundamental mismatch
Chinese specialty chemical competition is structurally pressuring margins; the 2022 peak was a COVID-era aberration, not the new normal
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The specialty chemicals boom of FY22 (net profit INR 1,186 Cr) was a one-time gift from supply chain disruptions — the market priced it as permanent, and the stock never fully de-rated when reality intervened. Now at INR 441, you are paying 43x earnings for a business earning 6% ROE with contracting EBITDA (FY22: INR 1,687 Cr → FY25: INR 986 Cr) and no free cash flow. This is the second-level question: analysts are bullish on recovery, forward P/E of 28x assumes significant margin expansion — but that is precisely the consensus that is already priced in.

The structural issue is Chinese overcapacity in benzene-chain intermediates, which is not a temporary headwind. Aarti has been investing heavily (INR 1,300-1,400 Cr capex annually) with CWIP of INR 1,596 Cr, betting on a demand recovery that may arrive later and shallower than expected. Meanwhile, rising interest costs eat into a thin earnings base. At 18.4x EV/EBITDA, the stock needs perfect execution on the recovery thesis to merely justify current prices — there is no margin of safety. I would not pay 43x for 6% ROE under any circumstances.
